Sell My House Fast in Jacksonville, FL: Options, Costs and Cash Offers

Cash Home Buyers in Florida
Cash Offer in 24 Hours
  • Inherited, behind on payments, tenants, repairs: we buy it as-is
  • Zero fees, zero commissions, zero closing costs
  • No obligation: turn the offer down and owe us nothing

Sell Your Jacksonville House for Cash

Tell us about your Jacksonville house. We buy as-is and reply with a written cash offer.

Call or Text  (424) 435-2326


Last updated November 14, 2026. Citations come from the Florida statutes and official agency pages linked in Sources. Where we could not confirm something on an official page, we say so.

Selling a house in Jacksonville, Florida comes down to a choice between listing it, selling it yourself and taking a cash offer. Each route has different costs and timelines under Florida law, and this guide lays them out with official sources. Jacksonville had an estimated 1,017,689 residents in 2025, and the Census Bureau puts the median value of an owner-occupied home at $266,100 in its 2019-2023 survey. We did not use listing-site price data.

Jacksonville housing at a glance

These figures come from the Census Bureau. They describe the city as a whole, not your street or your house. Jacksonville is in Duval County.

  • Estimated population, July 1, 2025: 1,017,689 (Census Bureau).
  • Median value of owner-occupied homes: $266,100 (American Community Survey, 2019-2023).
  • Owner-occupied homes: 220,976. Renter-occupied homes: 163,765, so about 57% of occupied homes are owner-occupied.
  • Median gross rent: $1,375 a month.
  • Median year homes were built: 1986.
  • Vacant housing units: 37,614 of 422,355 total.

Three ways to sell a house in Jacksonville

List with an agent. We did not find a Florida statute that sets a commission rate, so the rate is whatever your listing agreement says. You also pick up closing costs, repairs and showings. See Florida real estate commission and closing costs.

Sell it yourself. A Florida owner selling their own property is generally outside the broker licensing law. You still owe the buyer a flood disclosure at or before contract signing, a property tax disclosure summary and, for buildings, a radon notice. Details are in for sale by owner in Florida and Florida seller disclosures.

Take a cash offer. We buy houses as-is, with no agent commission, no fees and no closing costs charged to you. You choose the closing date, and the title company pays any mortgage and unpaid property tax from the proceeds.

Selling in Jacksonville?
We buy Jacksonville houses as-is, with no commission, no repairs and no closing costs to you.
Get My Cash Offer →

Situations we see with Jacksonville houses

Behind on the mortgage. Florida foreclosures go through court. After a final judgment, the court directs the clerk to hold a public sale on a set day, generally 20 to 35 days later, and the owner can redeem until the clerk files the certificate of sale (Fla. Stat. 45.031 and 45.0315). Read the Florida foreclosure process before you decide.

Inherited house. Who can sell depends on whether there is a will and how the estate is administered. Florida homestead also has devise limits. See probate, intestate succession, lady bird deeds and homestead protection.

Unpaid property tax. Florida property tax is due November 1 and delinquent April 1. See the Florida property tax guide and tax deed sales.

Tenants or squatters. Eviction, selling a rented house and squatter cases follow different Florida rules. Condo and HOA sellers should read about estoppel certificates.

Property tax when you sell in Jacksonville

Florida taxes are due November 1, or when the certified roll reaches the tax collector, and become delinquent April 1. Early payment discounts run 4 percent in November, 3 percent in December, 2 percent in January and 1 percent in February (Fla. Stat. 197.162 and 197.333). Real property is assessed as of January 1. We did not find an official source that gives one tax rate for all of Jacksonville, so we do not state one. Ask the county tax collector for the amount due in the month you expect to close, and give that figure to the title company.

Homeowners must apply for the homestead exemption with the county property appraiser by March 1, and a change of ownership ends the Save Our Homes cap. See the homestead exemption and property tax appeals.

Taxes on the sale itself

Florida does not impose a personal income tax, but federal capital gains rules can apply. The IRS lets you exclude up to $250,000 of gain on your main home, or $500,000 if married filing jointly, if you meet the ownership and use tests. Documentary stamp tax on a deed is 70 cents per $100 of consideration (Fla. Stat. 201.02). See capital gains on a home sale.

How to sell a house in Florida when you are in Jacksonville

  1. Find out what the title company needs. For an inherited or transferred house, that usually means the recorded document that shows who owns it today.
  2. Get a payoff for any mortgage and the amount of any unpaid property tax. Both are paid from the sale proceeds at closing.
  3. Compare offers on what you net after repairs, commissions and closing costs, not on the headline price.
  4. If you want a fast, simple closing, ask for a written cash offer. We buy houses as-is, with no repairs and no agent commission. See how we buy houses in Florida.

Selling a house in Jacksonville FAQ

Can I sell my Jacksonville house as-is?

Yes. Florida law does not require a seller to make repairs before listing, though you must give the required disclosures. A cash buyer purchases as-is.

How much is a house worth in Jacksonville?

The Census Bureau's 2019-2023 survey puts the median value of owner-occupied homes in Jacksonville at $266,100. Your house will differ, so get a written offer or an appraisal.

Do I pay a commission to sell for cash to you?

No. Our offers carry no agent commission, fees or closing costs to you.

Can I sell a Jacksonville house with a mortgage or unpaid taxes?

Yes. The title company pays the mortgage payoff and any unpaid property tax from the proceeds at closing.

Does Florida have a state income tax?

No. The Florida Department of Revenue says Florida does not impose a personal income tax. Federal tax rules can still apply to your gain.

Sell Your Titusville House for Cash

Tell us about your Titusville house. We buy as-is and reply with a written cash offer.

Call or Text  (424) 435-2326


Last updated November 14, 2026. Citations come from the Florida statutes and official agency pages linked in Sources. Where we could not confirm something on an official page, we say so.

Selling a house in Titusville, Florida comes down to a choice between listing it, selling it yourself and taking a cash offer. Each route has different costs and timelines under Florida law, and this guide lays them out with official sources. Titusville had an estimated 49,800 residents in 2025, and the Census Bureau puts the median value of an owner-occupied home at $243,100 in its 2019-2023 survey. We did not use listing-site price data.

Titusville housing at a glance

These figures come from the Census Bureau. They describe the city as a whole, not your street or your house. Titusville is in Brevard County.

  • Estimated population, July 1, 2025: 49,800 (Census Bureau).
  • Median value of owner-occupied homes: $243,100 (American Community Survey, 2019-2023).
  • Owner-occupied homes: 14,161. Renter-occupied homes: 5,484, so about 72% of occupied homes are owner-occupied.
  • Median gross rent: $1,281 a month.
  • Median year homes were built: 1982.
  • Vacant housing units: 4,160 of 23,805 total.

Three ways to sell a house in Titusville

List with an agent. We did not find a Florida statute that sets a commission rate, so the rate is whatever your listing agreement says. You also pick up closing costs, repairs and showings. See Florida real estate commission and closing costs.

Sell it yourself. A Florida owner selling their own property is generally outside the broker licensing law. You still owe the buyer a flood disclosure at or before contract signing, a property tax disclosure summary and, for buildings, a radon notice. Details are in for sale by owner in Florida and Florida seller disclosures.

Take a cash offer. We buy houses as-is, with no agent commission, no fees and no closing costs charged to you. You choose the closing date, and the title company pays any mortgage and unpaid property tax from the proceeds.

Selling in Titusville?
We buy Titusville houses as-is, with no commission, no repairs and no closing costs to you.
Get My Cash Offer →

Situations we see with Titusville houses

Behind on the mortgage. Florida foreclosures go through court. After a final judgment, the court directs the clerk to hold a public sale on a set day, generally 20 to 35 days later, and the owner can redeem until the clerk files the certificate of sale (Fla. Stat. 45.031 and 45.0315). Read the Florida foreclosure process before you decide.

Inherited house. Who can sell depends on whether there is a will and how the estate is administered. Florida homestead also has devise limits. See probate, intestate succession, lady bird deeds and homestead protection.

Unpaid property tax. Florida property tax is due November 1 and delinquent April 1. See the Florida property tax guide and tax deed sales.

Tenants or squatters. Eviction, selling a rented house and squatter cases follow different Florida rules. Condo and HOA sellers should read about estoppel certificates.

Property tax when you sell in Titusville

Florida taxes are due November 1, or when the certified roll reaches the tax collector, and become delinquent April 1. Early payment discounts run 4 percent in November, 3 percent in December, 2 percent in January and 1 percent in February (Fla. Stat. 197.162 and 197.333). Real property is assessed as of January 1. We did not find an official source that gives one tax rate for all of Titusville, so we do not state one. Ask the county tax collector for the amount due in the month you expect to close, and give that figure to the title company.

Homeowners must apply for the homestead exemption with the county property appraiser by March 1, and a change of ownership ends the Save Our Homes cap. See the homestead exemption and property tax appeals.

Taxes on the sale itself

Florida does not impose a personal income tax, but federal capital gains rules can apply. The IRS lets you exclude up to $250,000 of gain on your main home, or $500,000 if married filing jointly, if you meet the ownership and use tests. Documentary stamp tax on a deed is 70 cents per $100 of consideration (Fla. Stat. 201.02). See capital gains on a home sale.

How to sell a house in Florida when you are in Titusville

  1. Find out what the title company needs. For an inherited or transferred house, that usually means the recorded document that shows who owns it today.
  2. Get a payoff for any mortgage and the amount of any unpaid property tax. Both are paid from the sale proceeds at closing.
  3. Compare offers on what you net after repairs, commissions and closing costs, not on the headline price.
  4. If you want a fast, simple closing, ask for a written cash offer. We buy houses as-is, with no repairs and no agent commission. See how we buy houses in Florida.

Selling a house in Titusville FAQ

Can I sell my Titusville house as-is?

Yes. Florida law does not require a seller to make repairs before listing, though you must give the required disclosures. A cash buyer purchases as-is.

How much is a house worth in Titusville?

The Census Bureau's 2019-2023 survey puts the median value of owner-occupied homes in Titusville at $243,100. Your house will differ, so get a written offer or an appraisal.

Do I pay a commission to sell for cash to you?

No. Our offers carry no agent commission, fees or closing costs to you.

Can I sell a Titusville house with a mortgage or unpaid taxes?

Yes. The title company pays the mortgage payoff and any unpaid property tax from the proceeds at closing.

Does Florida have a state income tax?

No. The Florida Department of Revenue says Florida does not impose a personal income tax. Federal tax rules can still apply to your gain.

Last updated November 14, 2026. Citations come from the Florida statutes and official agency pages linked in Sources. Where we could not confirm something on an official page, we say so.

Selling a house in Groveland, Florida comes down to a choice between listing it, selling it yourself and taking a cash offer. Each route has different costs and timelines under Florida law, and this guide lays them out with official sources. Groveland had an estimated 25,526 residents in 2025, and the Census Bureau puts the median value of an owner-occupied home at $344,000 in its 2019-2023 survey. We did not use listing-site price data.

Groveland housing at a glance

These figures come from the Census Bureau. They describe the city as a whole, not your street or your house. Groveland is in Lake County.

  • Estimated population, July 1, 2025: 25,526 (Census Bureau).
  • Median value of owner-occupied homes: $344,000 (American Community Survey, 2019-2023).
  • Owner-occupied homes: 6,387. Renter-occupied homes: 913, so about 87% of occupied homes are owner-occupied.
  • Median gross rent: $1,579 a month.
  • Median year homes were built: 2010.
  • Vacant housing units: 448 of 7,748 total.

Three ways to sell a house in Groveland

List with an agent. We did not find a Florida statute that sets a commission rate, so the rate is whatever your listing agreement says. You also pick up closing costs, repairs and showings. See Florida real estate commission and closing costs.

Sell it yourself. A Florida owner selling their own property is generally outside the broker licensing law. You still owe the buyer a flood disclosure at or before contract signing, a property tax disclosure summary and, for buildings, a radon notice. Details are in for sale by owner in Florida and Florida seller disclosures.

Take a cash offer. We buy houses as-is, with no agent commission, no fees and no closing costs charged to you. You choose the closing date, and the title company pays any mortgage and unpaid property tax from the proceeds.

Selling in Groveland?
We buy Groveland houses as-is, with no commission, no repairs and no closing costs to you.
Get My Cash Offer →

Situations we see with Groveland houses

Behind on the mortgage. Florida foreclosures go through court. After a final judgment, the court directs the clerk to hold a public sale on a set day, generally 20 to 35 days later, and the owner can redeem until the clerk files the certificate of sale (Fla. Stat. 45.031 and 45.0315). Read the Florida foreclosure process before you decide.

Inherited house. Who can sell depends on whether there is a will and how the estate is administered. Florida homestead also has devise limits. See probate, intestate succession, lady bird deeds and homestead protection.

Unpaid property tax. Florida property tax is due November 1 and delinquent April 1. See the Florida property tax guide and tax deed sales.

Tenants or squatters. Eviction, selling a rented house and squatter cases follow different Florida rules. Condo and HOA sellers should read about estoppel certificates.

Property tax when you sell in Groveland

Florida taxes are due November 1, or when the certified roll reaches the tax collector, and become delinquent April 1. Early payment discounts run 4 percent in November, 3 percent in December, 2 percent in January and 1 percent in February (Fla. Stat. 197.162 and 197.333). Real property is assessed as of January 1. We did not find an official source that gives one tax rate for all of Groveland, so we do not state one. Ask the county tax collector for the amount due in the month you expect to close, and give that figure to the title company.

Homeowners must apply for the homestead exemption with the county property appraiser by March 1, and a change of ownership ends the Save Our Homes cap. See the homestead exemption and property tax appeals.

Taxes on the sale itself

Florida does not impose a personal income tax, but federal capital gains rules can apply. The IRS lets you exclude up to $250,000 of gain on your main home, or $500,000 if married filing jointly, if you meet the ownership and use tests. Documentary stamp tax on a deed is 70 cents per $100 of consideration (Fla. Stat. 201.02). See capital gains on a home sale.

How to sell a house in Florida when you are in Groveland

  1. Find out what the title company needs. For an inherited or transferred house, that usually means the recorded document that shows who owns it today.
  2. Get a payoff for any mortgage and the amount of any unpaid property tax. Both are paid from the sale proceeds at closing.
  3. Compare offers on what you net after repairs, commissions and closing costs, not on the headline price.
  4. If you want a fast, simple closing, ask for a written cash offer. We buy houses as-is, with no repairs and no agent commission. See how we buy houses in Florida.

Selling a house in Groveland FAQ

Can I sell my Groveland house as-is?

Yes. Florida law does not require a seller to make repairs before listing, though you must give the required disclosures. A cash buyer purchases as-is.

How much is a house worth in Groveland?

The Census Bureau's 2019-2023 survey puts the median value of owner-occupied homes in Groveland at $344,000. Your house will differ, so get a written offer or an appraisal.

Do I pay a commission to sell for cash to you?

No. Our offers carry no agent commission, fees or closing costs to you.

Can I sell a Groveland house with a mortgage or unpaid taxes?

Yes. The title company pays the mortgage payoff and any unpaid property tax from the proceeds at closing.

Does Florida have a state income tax?

No. The Florida Department of Revenue says Florida does not impose a personal income tax. Federal tax rules can still apply to your gain.
